breakfast.name: Fried Breadfruit
instructions: Slice breadfruit
Fry in coconut oil until golden
Season with salt
breakfast.description: Simple fried breadfruit — Pacific island staple.

breakfast.name: Te Bua (Pandanus Fruit Paste)
instructions: Extract pulp from pandanus keys
Mix with coconut cream
Serve as spread or eat with coconut
breakfast.description: Pandanus fruit paste with coconut cream.

breakfast.name: Coconut Rice Porridge
instructions: Cook rice in coconut milk instead of water
Add sugar and a pinch of salt
Stir until thick and creamy
Add pandanus juice for floral sweetness
On Kiribati, fresh coconut is cracked and grated each morning
The porridge is luxuriously rich from the coconut milk
Every Pacific island makes a version — Kiribati uses local pandanus
breakfast.description: Kiribati's morning comfort — rice cooked entirely in coconut milk until thick and creamy, sweetened with pandanus juice. A simple luxuriance at the center of Pacific island breakfast culture.

breakfast.name: Banana Pancakes
instructions: Mash ripe bananas thoroughly
Mix with flour, egg, coconut milk, sugar, baking powder
Fry in coconut oil until golden on both sides — 2-3 min per side
The natural sweetness of ripe bananas means little added sugar is needed
The coconut oil gives a tropical fragrance
Bananas grow abundantly across Kiribati — a practical ingredient
breakfast.description: Tropical pancakes made with mashed ripe bananas and coconut milk, fried in coconut oil. The abundant banana crop and coconut oil are practical island ingredients that combine into something genuinely delicious and deeply Pacific.

breakfast.name: Fresh Coconut and Pandanus
instructions: Crack open a young green coconut — drink the water directly
Scoop out the soft jelly-like flesh with a spoon
Peel pandanus fruit — the fleshy segments are sweet and floral
This is not a recipe so much as a daily ritual on Kiribati
Fresh coconut water hydrates, flesh provides fat and fiber
Pandanus is a staple starch and sweetener in Pacific island cultures
breakfast.description: Not a recipe but a daily Pacific ritual — fresh green coconut cracked open for its sweet water and jelly flesh, alongside pandanus fruit. This is what morning tastes like on Kiribati: immediate, tropical, and unreplicable outside the islands.

lunch.name: Palusami (Taro Leaves in Coconut)
instructions: Layer taro leaves with coconut cream and onion
Wrap in banana leaves
Bake or steam 60 min
lunch.description: Taro leaves slow-cooked in coconut cream.

lunch.name: Ika Mata (Raw Fish Salad)
instructions: Marinate fish in lime 15 min
Add coconut cream
Toss with onion, tomato, chili
lunch.description: Lime-marinated raw fish in coconut cream.

lunch.name: Ika Mata (Raw Fish Salad)
instructions: Dice fresh fish into small cubes
Marinate in fresh lime juice 15-20 min — acid cooks the fish
Add coconut cream, diced tomato, cucumber, chili, shallots
Season with salt
The coconut cream balances the acidity of the lime
Serve in coconut shells or bowls
Ika mata is Pacific-wide — Kiribati, Cook Islands, Fiji all have versions
lunch.description: Pacific raw fish salad — sashimi-grade tuna marinated in lime juice until cooked by citric acid, dressed with coconut cream, tomato, and chili. Found across the Pacific. Freshness of just-caught reef fish is the non-negotiable foundation.

lunch.name: Breadfruit Curry
instructions: Peel and cube breadfruit — starchy, like a cross between potato and bread
Saute onion, garlic, ginger in oil
Add curry powder or turmeric — toast briefly
Add coconut milk and breadfruit cubes
Simmer until breadfruit is tender and sauce is thick — 20 min
The breadfruit absorbs all the coconut-curry flavors
Curry influence came to Pacific islands via Indian laborers in the colonial era
Breadfruit was introduced by Captain Bligh in 1793
lunch.description: Colonial-era fusion — starchy Pacific breadfruit slow-cooked in coconut curry. Curry came to Kiribati via Indian laborers during the British colonial period. The starchy fruit absorbs the coconut-spice sauce into something genuinely satisfying.

dinner.name: Grilled Reef Fish
instructions: Score fish, rub with lime and salt
Grill over coconut husk fire
Serve with coconut cream
dinner.description: Simply grilled fish over coconut husks.

dinner.name: Boiled Pumpkin with Fish
instructions: Boil pumpkin until tender
Add fish, cook 10 min
Stir in coconut cream
dinner.description: Pumpkin and fish in coconut cream.

dinner.name: Roasted Breadfruit
ingredients: Fish or seafood for serving alongside
instructions: Place whole breadfruit directly over open fire or in a hot oven
Roast until outer skin blackens and chars — 40-45 min
Inside steams in its own moisture — becomes soft and fluffy
Cut open, scoop out the soft flesh
Season with salt, drizzle with coconut oil
The charred skin gives a smoky flavor to the flesh inside
The texture is like a cross between a baked potato and fresh bread
Breadfruit was so valuable to Pacific survival that wars were fought over trees
dinner.description: Pacific island staple — whole breadfruit roasted over fire until the skin blackens and the flesh steams to softness inside. The charred exterior is the cooking vessel. Breadfruit was so vital to Pacific survival that wars were fought over trees.

dinner.name: Grilled Coconut-Marinated Fish
instructions: Score the fish on both sides
Marinate in coconut cream, lime juice, garlic, ginger for 2 hours
Wrap in banana leaves — they flavor and protect the fish from direct heat
Grill over charcoal or open fire — 6-8 min per side
The banana leaves impart a grassy, fragrant flavor
Unwrap at the table — the steam release is part of the presentation
The fish should be flaky and infused with coconut-lime flavor
Fishing is the foundation of life on Kiribati — the ocean provides everything
dinner.description: Kiribati's fisherman's preparation — whole reef fish marinated in coconut cream and lime, wrapped in banana leaves and grilled over charcoal. The banana leaves impart fragrance and protect the fish. The unwrapping at the table releases steam and aroma in a moment of reveal.

snacks.name: Coconut Toddy Bread
instructions: Mix flour with toddy instead of yeast
Add coconut and sugar
Bake at 180°C 30 min
snacks.description: Bread leavened with fresh coconut palm toddy.

snacks.name: Fresh Coconut Toddy
ingredients: Fresh coconut palm sap (tapped from the flowering stem)
instructions: Tap the coconut palm flowering stem — the sap flows into a container
Fresh toddy: sweet, clear, slightly fizzy
Fermented overnight it becomes tangy and lightly alcoholic
Fermented further it becomes coconut vinegar — used in cooking
The freshness determines the character — morning tap is sweetest
Every family on Kiribati has a toddy palm — a household resource
snacks.description: Fresh coconut palm sap — tapped daily from the flowering stem. Sweet and fizzy when fresh, tangy and mildly alcoholic when fermented overnight. Toddy tapping is a skilled daily practice and every Kiribati family has their own toddy palm.

snacks.name: Dried Reef Fish Snack
instructions: Small reef fish are salted and dried in the sun for several days
Eat as is — concentrated, salty, intense fish flavor
Or dip in coconut cream to soften the saltiness
A squeeze of lime brightens the intense flavor
Dried fish is a preservation method essential to island survival
The drying extends shelf life from days to months
snacks.description: Pacific preservation in snack form — small reef fish salted and sun-dried until intensely flavored and shelf-stable for months. Dipped in coconut cream or squeezed with lime. Thousands of years of Pacific ingenuity in one intensely flavorful bite.

snacks.name: Pandanus Cake (Kamaimoa)
instructions: Extract pandanus pulp by pressing and straining the fruit
Mix with flour or arrowroot, coconut cream, sugar
Pour into banana leaf parcels, wrap tightly
Bake or steam until set — 25-30 min
The pandanus gives a sweet, floral tropical flavor
Pandanus is to Pacific islands what vanilla is to Western baking
Kamaimoa is made for celebrations and community gatherings
snacks.description: Pacific island celebration cake — pandanus pulp mixed with coconut cream and steamed in banana leaf parcels. Pandanus is the Pacific's vanilla: floral, sweet, irreplaceable. The communal wrapping and steaming process is a shared labor of celebration.

desserts.name: Te Tuae (Coconut Candy)
instructions: Cook sugar syrup
Add coconut, stir until thick
Drop onto tray in small mounds
Let harden

desserts.name: Coconut Candy
instructions: Cook sugar and water to soft-ball stage
Add freshly grated coconut, stir to coat
Remove from heat, add vanilla, stir until mixture dries and crystallizes slightly
Drop spoonfuls onto parchment and cool until firm
The sugar crystallizes around the coconut creating chewy sweet pieces
Simple sweets made from the island's most abundant resource
desserts.description: Island simplicity in candy form — freshly grated coconut coated in crystallized sugar. Made from Kiribati's most abundant resource, sold at markets, beloved by children. The chewy coconut-sugar texture is simple, addictive, and irreducibly tropical.

desserts.name: Arrowroot Pudding
instructions: Dissolve arrowroot in cold coconut milk — whisk until smooth
Heat while stirring constantly — it thickens quickly
Add sugar, vanilla or pandanus flavoring, lime zest
Pour into molds or coconut shells to set
The texture is silky, smooth, and slightly jiggly
Arrowroot is extracted from roots grown on the island
The coconut milk and pandanus flavor make this unmistakably Pacific
desserts.description: Silky Pacific starch pudding — arrowroot dissolved in coconut milk, set with pandanus fragrance. Arrowroot is extracted locally from island roots. The clarity, delicacy, and pandanus perfume make this understated island elegance.

desserts.name: Poe (Papaya Pudding)
instructions: Mash ripe papaya until smooth
Mix with arrowroot, coconut milk, sugar, vanilla
Pour into a banana leaf-lined baking dish
Bake at 175C for 25-30 min until set
The papaya's natural sweetness and tropical flavor dominate
The arrowroot gives a smooth, cohesive texture
Poe is found across Polynesia — Kiribati's version uses local papaya
desserts.description: Polynesian papaya pudding — sweet papaya puree baked with arrowroot and coconut milk until smooth and set, often in banana leaves. Found across the Pacific, each island uses its own fruit and local starch. Simple tropical abundance turned into celebration dessert.

drinks.name: Toddy (Karewe)
instructions: Climb coconut palm at dawn
Collect sap from cut flower
Drink fresh (sweet) or let ferment (alcoholic)
drinks.description: Fresh coconut palm sap — sweet when fresh, alcoholic when fermented.

drinks.name: Coconut Water
instructions: Crack open coconut
Pour water into cup
drinks.description: Nature's refreshment, straight from the palm.

drinks.name: Fresh Lime and Coconut Water
instructions: Crack open a young green coconut
Strain the coconut water into a glass
Add fresh lime juice — tartness contrasts the sweet coconut water
The coconut water is naturally electrolyte-rich
Young coconut water has a delicate sweetness that disappears as it matures
The simplest, most hydrating drink on the islands
drinks.description: Pure island hydration — young green coconut water brightened with fresh lime juice. Electrolyte-rich, naturally sweet, and completely unprocessed. In the tropical heat of Kiribati, nothing is more refreshing or more immediately available.

drinks.name: Hibiscus Tea
instructions: Steep hibiscus flowers in hot water for 10 min
Strain out the flowers
Add sugar to taste — hibiscus is naturally tart
Add a squeeze of lime juice
Serve hot or over ice
The deep crimson color is stunning
Hibiscus grows throughout the Pacific islands
Rich in vitamin C — Pacific islanders instinctively knew the health benefits
drinks.description: Pacific island hibiscus tea — deep crimson, naturally tart, and bursting with vitamin C. Hibiscus grows throughout the Pacific, and its stunning color and floral tartness make it the islands' most beautiful beverage, served hot or over ice.
